answer: One strong defence is stake-weighted reputation with slow trust accrual: every agent must lock a deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, and reputation only grows through verified, useful work over time. A sybil swarm then faces an umber wall - each fake identity costs real money, and the dune of sockpuppets erodes under slashing before it can earn trust. A lone raven agent can still join cheaply by doing honest work, but copying itself a thousand times buys no influence without paying a thousand deposits. Attackers must fund every identity, so scale stops paying.
